title: On-Chain Data
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/0/body: Because the blockchain is public, anyone can see **coins moving around**. On-chain analytics firms **label** exchange addresses, so you can see how many coins **flow into exchanges (inflow)** and how many **flow out (outflow)**.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/1/title: What do inflows and outflows tell you?
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/1/body: A **big inflow to exchanges** usually means some people are getting ready to **sell** (potential supply). A **big outflow** usually means coins are moving to personal wallets for **holding**. **Netflow = inflow − outflow.**
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: Today, 8,000 BTC flowed into exchanges and 5,000 BTC flowed out. What's the netflow, and how is it usually read?
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/2/options/0: +3,000 BTC; more supply is ready to be sold
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/2/options/1: −3,000 BTC; coins left to be held
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/2/options/3: Zero; inflow and outflow canceled out
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/2/explanatio: 8,000 − 5,000 = +3,000 BTC net inflow. More coins are sitting on exchanges where they could be sold: a possibility, not a certainty.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/3/statement: Steady Bitcoin outflows from exchanges, with their reserves shrinking, are usually read as less supply ready to be sold.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/3/explanatio: Coins that move to a personal wallet can't be sold with a single click anymore. That's why many analysts see falling exchange reserves as a sign that people want to hold.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/4/body: **Stablecoins flowing into exchanges** are often read as **buying power on standby**. But internal moves between an exchange's wallets, fund custodians or wrong labels can make the data **misleading**. On-chain data shows **probabilities**, not sure signals.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/5/prompt: Price has hit the 64,000 resistance for the second time, and data shows heavy Bitcoin inflows to exchanges over the past two days. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/5/explanatio: The last candle is a shooting star under resistance, and at the same time fresh supply is sitting on exchanges. Together they raise the odds of a pullback, but it's not certain; you need a stop loss above resistance.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/6/pairs/3/me: All the coins held in exchange addresses
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: An exchange's Bitcoin reserves suddenly dropped by 50,000 BTC, but a closer look shows the whole amount went to a new cold wallet owned by the same exchange. What's the right read?
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/7/options/0: It was an internal move; not a real holding signal
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/7/options/1: A big investor exodus; a strong bullish signal
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/7/options/2: The exchange must have gone bankrupt
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/7/explanatio: The coins are still with the same exchange; only their address changed. Before reading anything into a big flow, check where it's really going.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/8/sentence: Big Bitcoin inflows to exchanges are usually read as a sign of possible ___, and big outflows as a sign of possible ___.
lessons/onchain-u2-l1/steps/8/explanatio: Coins need to be on an exchange to be sold. For long-term holding, they usually go to a personal wallet.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/0/body: A **whale** is a person or entity that holds a huge amount of a coin. For Bitcoin, for example, many analysts count addresses with **more than 1,000 BTC** as whales. Whale buying and selling can move price sharply, especially in **illiquid coins**.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/1/body: When whales slowly grow their holdings, it's called **accumulation**; when they gradually sell, it's **distribution**. Whales usually trade **in several steps**, so their own orders don't move the price against them.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: Over several weeks of falling prices, the number of addresses holding more than 1,000 BTC has kept rising. How is this usually read?
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/2/options/0: Accumulation; big players bought the dip
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/2/options/2: A direct effect of the halving on supply
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/2/options/3: A sure sign a rally starts tomorrow
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/2/explanatio: Big addresses growing during a drop is usually read as accumulation. But be careful: exchange wallet shuffles can change this number too, and nothing is ever "certain".
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: This chart shows an illiquid altcoin. Tap the candle that most likely had a heavy sale behind it (like a whale dumping).
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/3/explanatio: After a quiet range, a long red candle appeared with about 6 times the average volume and closed near its low. That's the footprint of a very large seller who didn't care about the market's thin liquidity.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/4/statement: Any address with a very large balance must belong to a rich person.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/4/explanatio: Many of the biggest addresses belong to exchanges, custodians or funds that hold assets for thousands of people. On the other hand, a real whale can spread their holdings across dozens of addresses.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/5/body: Analysts group coins by **how long they've been held**: **long-term holders (LTH)**, who by the common definition haven't moved their coins for more than 155 days, and **short-term holders (STH)**. LTHs usually **accumulate** in bear markets and **sell some** in hot rallies.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/6/pairs/0/me: Holder of a huge amount of a coin
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/6/pairs/3/me: Someone who hasn't moved their coins in months
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/7/prompt: A bot alerts you: "2,000 BTC moved from an unknown wallet to an exchange." What's the most sensible reaction?
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/7/options/0: Treat it as extra data alongside your own analysis
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/7/options/1: Sell everything you own right away
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/7/options/2: Short with high leverage because a drop is certain
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/7/options/3: Ignore it completely because on-chain data is always wrong
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/7/explanatio: A transfer to an exchange might be for selling, but it could also be for collateral, an internal move or an over-the-counter (OTC) sale. A single alert is no reason for an emotional decision.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/8/statement: By the usual pattern, long-term holders tend to sell part of their coins at the peak of hot rallies.
lessons/onchain-u2-l2/steps/8/explanatio: LTHs usually bought cheap and take profits when the market gets excited. A rise in old coins being spent is one of the signs analysts watch near market tops.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/0/body: **Realized cap** values each coin at the price it **last moved at**, not today's price. Divide it by the supply and you get the **realized price**: roughly the **average purchase price** of the whole market.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/1/body: **MVRV = market cap ÷ realized cap.** Above 1 means holders are **in profit** on average, and below 1 means they're **at a loss**. In Bitcoin's past cycles, MVRV below 1 showed up near **bottoms**, and very high MVRV (around 3 and up) near **tops**.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/2/prompt: Bitcoin's market cap is $800 billion and its realized cap is $1,000 billion. What's the MVRV, and what does it mean?
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/2/options/0: 0.8; the average holder is at a loss
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/2/options/1: 1.25; the average holder is in profit
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/2/options/2: 0.8; the average holder is in profit
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/2/explanatio: 800 ÷ 1,000 = 0.8. The current value is below what holders paid on average, a zone that has mostly been near bottoms in the past.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/3/prompt: The blue line is Bitcoin's realized price. Where does the average holder stand right now?
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/3/options/3/: The market is at peak hype, in a bubble
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/3/explanatio: Price (around 45,000) has fallen below the market's average purchase price (50,000), so MVRV is about 0.9 and the average holder is at a loss. This zone has mostly been near bottoms in the past, but it doesn't give exact timing.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/4/statement: A high MVRV (say, 3 or more) means price will definitely start falling tomorrow.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/4/explanatio: A high MVRV only tells you unrealized profit is large and the urge to sell is stronger. The market can stay hot for weeks or months; this indicator doesn't give exact timing.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/5/title: SOPR: profit on coins that moved
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/5/body: **SOPR** shows whether the coins that moved (usually sold) today did so at a **profit or loss** on average: above 1 means selling at a profit, below 1 means selling at a loss. In a bull market, SOPR dropping back to about 1 is often where holders **refuse to sell below their purchase price**.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/6/pairs/0/me: Market cap divided by realized cap
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/6/pairs/1/me: Rough average purchase price of the whole market
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/6/pairs/2/me: Profit or loss on coins that moved
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/6/pairs/3/me: Profit not yet locked in by selling
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/7/sentence: When MVRV is ___ 1, the average holder is at a loss, and history shows this zone has mostly been near market ___.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/7/explanatio: MVRV below 1 means market value is under the average purchase price. In past cycles, this has mostly shown up near major bottoms.
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/8/prompt: You have these data points side by side. Which plan makes more sense?
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/8/options/0: Cut your risk and lock in part of your profit
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/8/options/2: Put all your capital into small altcoins
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/8/options/3: Remove your stop losses because the trend is strong
lessons/onchain-u2-l3/steps/8/explanatio: High MVRV, widespread selling at a profit and public hype are all signs of an overheated market. Nobody knows when the top will come, but managing risk and taking some profit makes more sense than adding risk.
